| stats count as bank | eval bank=split( "987654321111111 811111111111119 234234234234278 818181911112111", " ") | mvexpand bank,"

We start by bringing in the example data.
Next we want to select our first digit.",1,AdventOfCode25 Day 3<-O->part 1

| stats count as bank | eval bank=split( "987654321111111 811111111111119 234234234234278 818181911112111", " ") | mvexpand bank | eval digit1 = max( split( substr( bank, 1, len(bank) - 1 ), "" ) ),"

The first digit is obviously the most important, so we always want the highest one available, but we need to reserve at least one digit at the end of the bank for the second digit.
So take the bank, remove the last digit, and find the highest digit.",2,AdventOfCode25 Day 3<-O->part 1

| stats count as bank | eval bank=split( "987654321111111 811111111111119 234234234234278 818181911112111", " ") | mvexpand bank | eval digit1 = max( split( substr( bank, 1, len(bank) - 1 ), "" ) ) | eval digit1_index = mvfind( split( bank, "" ), digit1 ),"

Now for the second digit, we first need to figure out what options we have. How much of the bank is still available. For that we first need to find where digit1 is in bank.",3,AdventOfCode25 Day 3<-O->part 1

| stats count as bank | eval bank=split( "987654321111111 811111111111119 234234234234278 818181911112111", " ") | mvexpand bank | eval digit1 = max( split( substr( bank, 1, len(bank) - 1 ), "" ) ) | eval digit1_index = mvfind( split( bank, "" ), digit1 ) | eval digit2_candidates = substr( bank, digit1_index + 2, len(bank) ),"

And get the leftover usable bank which will be candidates for digit2.
Warning: mvfind uses a 0-based index whilst substr uses a 1-based index.",4,AdventOfCode25 Day 3<-O->part 1

| stats count as bank | eval bank=split( "987654321111111 811111111111119 234234234234278 818181911112111", " ") | mvexpand bank | eval digit1 = max( split( substr( bank, 1, len(bank) - 1 ), "" ) ) | eval digit1_index = mvfind( split( bank, "" ), digit1 ) | eval digit2_candidates = substr( bank, digit1_index + 2, len(bank) ) | eval digit2 = max( split( digit2_candidates, "" ) ) | eval joltage = digit1 . digit2,"

Now we can easily find digit2 and put things together.
Note: if there is more than one match, we want the first one. Thankfully, the docs say: ""If a match exists, the index of the first matching value is returned"".",5,AdventOfCode25 Day 3<-O->part 1

| stats count as bank | eval bank=split( "987654321111111 811111111111119 234234234234278 818181911112111", " ") | mvexpand bank | eval digit1 = max( split( substr( bank, 1, len(bank) - 1 ), "" ) ) | eval digit1_index = mvfind( split( bank, "" ), digit1 ) | eval digit2_candidates = substr( bank, digit1_index + 2, len(bank) ) | eval digit2 = max( split( digit2_candidates, "" ) ) | eval joltage = digit1 . digit2 | stats sum(joltage),"

The solution should be 357. It works!

Part 1 solved!

",6,AdventOfCode25 Day 3<-O->part 1

| inputlookup adventofcode2025day3.csv | eval digit1 = max( split( substr( bank, 1, len(bank) - 1 ), "" ) ) | eval digit1_index = mvfind( split( bank, "" ), digit1 ) | eval digit2_candidates = substr( bank, digit1_index + 2, len(bank) ) | eval digit2 = max( split( digit2_candidates, "" ) ) | eval joltage = digit1 . digit2 | stats sum(joltage),

And it scales with the full challenge data. The answer should be 17524.,7,AdventOfCode25 Day 3<-O->part 1 - full scale

| stats count as bank | eval bank=split( "987654321111111 811111111111119 234234234234278 818181911112111", " ") | mvexpand bank | eval digit1 = max( split( substr( bank, 1, len(bank) - 1 ), "" ) ) | eval digit1_index = mvfind( split( bank, "" ), digit1 ) | eval digit2_candidates = substr( bank, digit1_index + 2, len(bank) ) | eval digit2 = max( split( digit2_candidates, "" ) ) | eval joltage = digit1 . digit2 | stats sum(joltage),"

Now for part 2.

This is more of the same, but instead of 2-digit joltages, we now need 12-digit joltages. So that means the first digit will be the highest digit in the bank once we ring-fenced the last 11 digits. Then whatever is left (should be at least 11 digits, but probably more), we need to do the same but this time reserving the last 10 digits. And so on.
Of course, this is calling for a loop, but it can be paralysing to start there. Instead, it's easier to start with copy and paste.
Let's first go back to our example data.",8,AdventOfCode25 Day 3<-O->part 2

| stats count as bank | eval bank=split( "987654321111111 811111111111119 234234234234278 818181911112111", " ") | mvexpand bank | eval bank_orig = bank ``` just for debugging ``` | eval joltage = "" ``` First digit ``` | eval digit = max( split( substr( bank, 1, len(bank) - 1 ), "" ) ) | eval digit_index = mvfind( split( bank, "" ), digit ) | eval joltage = joltage . digit | eval bank = substr( bank, digit_index + 2, len(bank) ) ``` Last digit ``` | eval digit = max( split( bank, "" ) ) | eval joltage = joltage . digit | stats sum(joltage),"

Our first step is to rewrite what we've done in a cleaner way.
Note: we're keeping the sum at the end to make sure nothing changes in the results, but feel free to ""open in search"" and play without it.",9,AdventOfCode25 Day 3<-O->part 2

| stats count as bank | eval bank=split( "987654321111111 811111111111119 234234234234278 818181911112111", " ") | mvexpand bank | eval bank_orig = bank ``` just for debugging ``` | eval joltage = "" ``` First digit ``` | eval digit = max( split( substr( bank, 1, len(bank) - 1 ), "" ) ) | eval digit_index = mvfind( split( bank, "" ), digit ) | eval joltage = joltage . digit | eval bank = substr( bank, digit_index + 2, len(bank) ) ``` Last digit ``` | eval digit = max( split( substr( bank, 1, len(bank) - 0 ), "" ) ) | eval digit_index = mvfind( split( bank, "" ), digit ) | eval joltage = joltage . digit | eval bank = substr( bank, digit_index + 2, len(bank) ) | stats sum(joltage),"

Let's make that more evident by figuring out how we could do the second digit with as much of the same code as possible. What difference do we need to introduce?
Now what we need in our loop is becoming clearer.",10,AdventOfCode25 Day 3<-O->part 2

| stats count as bank | eval bank=split( "987654321111111 811111111111119 234234234234278 818181911112111", " ") | mvexpand bank | eval bank_orig = bank ``` just for debugging ``` | eval joltage = "" ``` First digit ``` | eval digit = max( split( substr( bank, 1, len(bank) - 1 ), "" ) ) | eval digit_index = mvfind( split( bank, "" ), digit ) | eval joltage = joltage . digit | eval bank = substr( bank, digit_index + 2, len(bank) ) ``` Last digit ``` | eval digit = max( split( substr( bank, 1, len(bank) - 0 ), "" ) ) | eval digit_index = mvfind( split( bank, "" ), digit ) | eval joltage = joltage . digit | eval bank = substr( bank, digit_index + 2, len(bank) ) | stats sum(joltage) | eval i=mvreverse( mvrange(0,2) ),"

Let's first work out our iterator on the side here.
Using mvreverse with mvrange is very clean.",11,AdventOfCode25 Day 3<-O->part 2

| stats count as bank | eval bank=split( "987654321111111 811111111111119 234234234234278 818181911112111", " ") | mvexpand bank | eval bank_orig = bank ``` just for debugging ``` | eval joltage = "" | eval i=mvreverse( mvrange(0,2) ) | foreach mode=multivalue i [| eval digit = max( split( substr( bank, 1, len(bank) - <> ), "" ) ) | eval digit_index = mvfind( split( bank, "" ), digit ) | eval joltage = joltage . digit | eval bank = substr( bank, digit_index + 2, len(bank) ) ] | stats sum(joltage),"

Now we are ready for the loop. It makes sense to usethe multivalue version of foreach, which refers to the iterated value inside the loop as <>.
Except foreach only supports a single eval command inside the loop. That's no problem though...",12,AdventOfCode25 Day 3<-O->part 2

| stats count as bank | eval bank=split( "987654321111111 811111111111119 234234234234278 818181911112111", " ") | mvexpand bank | eval bank_orig = bank ``` just for debugging ``` | eval joltage = "" | eval i=mvreverse( mvrange(0,2) ) | foreach mode=multivalue i [| eval digit = max( split( substr( bank, 1, len(bank) - <> ), "" ) ), digit_index = mvfind( split( bank, "" ), digit ), joltage = joltage . digit, bank = substr( bank, digit_index + 2, len(bank) ) ] | stats sum(joltage),"

The eval command supports multiple expressions (separated by commas) and will execute them in the right order, so this works.
If we were really good we could have been writing this version from the beginning, but notice how it was a lot less daunting doing it the way we did.",13,AdventOfCode25 Day 3<-O->part 2

| stats count as bank | eval bank=split( "987654321111111 811111111111119 234234234234278 818181911112111", " ") | mvexpand bank | eval bank_orig = bank ``` just for debugging ``` | eval joltage = "" | eval i=mvreverse( mvrange(0,12) ) | foreach mode=multivalue i [| eval digit = max( split( substr( bank, 1, len(bank) - <> ), "" ) ), digit_index = mvfind( split( bank, "" ), digit ), joltage = joltage . digit, bank = substr( bank, digit_index + 2, len(bank) ) ] | stats sum(joltage),"

All we have to do is change the number of times we iterate!
The correct answer is 3121910778619.

Part 2 solved!
